subject: Private VPC: responsibility runbook & latency evidence request
messages:
From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@cereslabs.io>
To: priyom_das@redwood.example, tessa_morgan@redwood.example
Cc: ops@cereslabs.io
Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private VPC: runbook & recent latency spikes

Hi Priyom / Tessa,

Thanks again for the quick onboarding last month. We ran into a couple of latency spikes during a scheduled edge maintenance window on Jun 20 that caused downstream inference tails to jump ~300ms for ~20 minutes. We're trying to reconcile responsibility so we can close the post-incident report.

Two asks to start:
- Can you share the operational runbook you expect us to follow for customer-controlled peering/NAT changes (what Redwood will monitor vs what we must notify in advance)?
- We attached a short sample of client-side latency traces (latency-sample-logs.txt). Can Redwood confirm whether the control plane or serving plane had any capacity throttles at the same time?

We also want to understand what carveouts Redwood expects for customer-managed edge routing (we manage the peering, ARP, and NAT). If those are excluded from the Private SLA, we need explicit language we can attach to our SOC2 evidence.

Can someone on your side send a draft responsibility matrix and any suggested amendment language? If easier, happy to schedule a quick 30 min call this week.

Thanks,
Sanjay
Sanjay Patel
Head of Platform | Ceres Labs
ops@cereslabs.io
Attachment: latency-sample-logs.txt (text)

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.example>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@cereslabs.io>
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.example, karthik_iyer@redwood.example, tessa_morgan@redwood.example
Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private VPC: runbook & recent latency spikes

Hi Sanjay — thanks for the note and for sending the logs. I pulled the control-plane and serving-plane metrics for Jun 20 and we don't see any autoscale or OOM events on the Dedicated pool that aligns with the 09:40–10:05 window in your traces, which suggests this is likely at the edge peering/NAT.

That said, we should be explicit in the runbook about responsibilities. High-level proposal (please review):
- Redwood (what we operate): host-side serving runtime, model versions pinned to customer config, control-plane rollout scheduling, kernel-level runtime updates, and failover to regional hosted variant when Dedicated capacity is constrained.
- Customer (what you operate): router/peering config, NAT translation, on-prem/firewall egress filtering, and physical colocation patch windows.

I'll attach a one-page draft runbook with notification thresholds and escalation steps (proposed_runbook_draft.pdf). Specific items we want from you:
- Confirm whether your edge team did any NAT translation changes or BGP flaps in the Jun 20 window.
- If you need carveouts in the SLA, specify exact events (BGP change, NAT rebind, firewall stateful reset) you want excluded and we can add language and evidence gating.

Happy to jump on a call — I'm free Tue/Wed morning PT.

—Priyom
Priyom Das
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachment: proposed_runbook_draft.pdf (one-pager)

From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@cereslabs.io>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.example>
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.example, karthik_iyer@redwood.example, tessa_morgan@redwood.example
Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private VPC: runbook & recent latency spikes

Thanks Priyom — copied our network lead (ops@cereslabs.io) who confirmed a NAT rebind at 09:47 for a rolling firmware update on our border router. We'll produce the change ticket.

Two follow-ups from Ceres:
1) For the incident window we are requesting an SLA credit if the spike is attributable to the Redwood path (please advise process + evidence to submit).
2) For future avoidance, we want explicit contract language that: (a) excludes customer-managed edge routing from Redwood availability/latency SLOs when we control peering/NAT, and (b) allows an agreed emergency fallback — e.g., Redwood automatically routes to a hosted variant for up to 1 hour if customer-side networking causes sustained latency over threshold.

Would Redwood accept an amendment similar to above? If so, please propose clause text and evidence gating. Otherwise we'll treat as procurement item in contract negotiations.

-Sanjay

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.example>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@cereslabs.io>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.example>, karthik_iyer@redwood.example, tessa_morgan@redwood.example
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 08:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private VPC: runbook & recent latency spikes

Hi Sanjay — Naomi from Product here. Appreciate the quick confirmation about the NAT rebind. To address your asks:

1) SLA credit path:
- Evidence we need from you: change ticket with timestamps, BGP session logs (if applicable), and the client traces you already supplied.
- Evidence we'll supply: serving node CPU/GPU utilization, control-plane rollout logs, autoscale events, and per-route latency histograms for the same window.
- Process: open a formal request (we prefer HubSpot ticket linked to deal_id DL-2026-0037). Our SLA committee evaluates within 5 business days and issues credit if responsibility is on our side.

2) Proposed amendment language (draft):
- "Customer-managed network components (including but not limited to BGP peering, NAT translation, and on-prem egress firewall rules) shall be excluded from Redwood Inference Private deployment latency and availability SLOs where the root cause is demonstrably attributable to such components. Redwood will provide diagnostic telemetry and cooperate in root cause analysis; automatic regional fallbacks to Redwood Hosted variants may be enacted per the fallback playbook defined below."

3) Fallback playbook (operational points):
- Trigger: 5-minute sustained P95 latency > 250ms at the customer ingress for 3 consecutive samples, with customer change ticket opening within the same window.
- Action: Redwood may route affected traffic to the nearest Hosted region variant for up to 1 hour while customer remedies the border issue.
- Billing: fallback duration beyond 1 hour will be billed at hosted-payg rates unless mutually agreed otherwise.

I've attached a short draft amendment doc (draft_amendment.docx) that folds this language into an SLA appendix. Please review and let us know the preferred approach to evidence exchange (we can set up an SFTP drop or use a secure share).

If that looks reasonable we can prepare formal contract wording and share for legal review.

Best,
Naomi
Product Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachment: draft_amendment.docx

From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@cereslabs.io>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.example>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.example>, karthik_iyer@redwood.example, tessa_morgan@redwood.example
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private VPC: runbook & recent latency spikes

Naomi / team — thanks, this is helpful and aligned with what we discussed internally. We'll pull together the change ticket and BGP logs (ops@cereslabs.io will drop into the SFTP).

Agreed on the fallback wording in principle; two asks before legal review:
- Can you add a small clause guaranteeing Redwood will notify us 10 minutes prior to enacting a regional fallback (we prefer an opt-out window for specific runtime-sensitive traffic)?
- For evidence exchange, SFTP with a TTL-limited share works for us; please send details.

Let's lock a 30-minute call Tue 09:30 PT to walk the amendment and SLA credit flow — ops and procurement will attend.

Appreciate the responsiveness.

-Sanjay
